ModMetaData.name: Grief
ModMetaData.author: T&B Modding
ModMetaData.description:
Losing someone should not be a mood penalty that quietly runs out.
In the base game, a colonist whose wife dies carries a flat penalty for thirty days and then is fine. This mod gives grief a shape instead.
Grief that changes over time - Shock, then raw grief, then an ache, then a dullness, and for the closest losses something that never entirely goes. - How hard it hits depends on who they were: a spouse or a child is not a colleague. Someone who had been with the colony for years is not someone who arrived last week. - It replaces the base game's flat penalty rather than adding to it.
Burial matters - Someone laid in a grave or a sarcophagus comes to rest, and the grief moves on. - Someone never recovered, butchered, or left lying about stays an open wound. The grief sticks and will not progress. - Burying them later resolves it, however long it has been.
The rest - Where it happened: standing in the room where someone died is hard for the first couple of weeks. - Survivor's guilt: being right there, unhurt, when someone else was not. - Anniversaries: a year on, it comes back for a day. - Shared grief: two colonists who lost the same person can sit with it together, which helps them both.
This mod only changes how colonists feel. It never changes how anyone aims, works or chooses a job.
Requires Harmony. Safe to add to an existing save. RimWorld 1.6, no DLC needed.
